He says the delegation has submitted its charter of demands and has been assured by the government that it would examine the issue and hold another meeting and address a press conference on the issue very soon.

Today we had a discussion in detail for two hours and we were assured that very soon we will again sit on this issue and have press conference and the government will take knowledge on this issue and some changes will be made which will be for the benefit of the country and to end the caste system and to move the country forward.

Soon J.P.
Nanda Ji.

JP Nadda has confirmed only cordial discussions and another meeting soon.
The government has announced no committee, no policy review and no changes to the existing reservation system.
Yet the political questions are already flying thick and fast.
CJP wants to know what is Prime Minister Modi's stand on this issue and opposition has already decided that this meeting is yet another proof that the BJP is anti-quota, anti-reservation.
They are basically against reservation of OBC and schedule cast.

RSS may be behind this movement.

The movement might be called.
Arakshan Hatao, Reservation Hatao, Remove Reservation, but the demands emerging from this movement are more nuanced.
They seek reform, not removal.
Correction, not elimination.
Economic need instead of caste as the basis.
A quota within quota, so benefits reach the most deprived.
A white paper assessing decades of reservation.
You can disagree with these propositions, but can you argue that they shouldn't even be debated?
After all, even courts have repeatedly held that reservation is not a fundamental right.
So why can't India at least debate whether the system needs a change, a reform, an overhaul?
And is there a deliberate attempt to confuse and conflate reform and removal for political purposes?
That's the big question.
Reservation is something guaranteed by the Constitution of India.
